title: Lupin III
synopsis: The grandson of the gentleman thief Arsène Lupin steals whatever he likes, with his gunman, his swordsman, the woman who always double-crosses him and the inspector who never gives up. 54 in the letters, reducing to 9.
body:
9Reduced, this title gives 9. It sits on The Closing with the rest of a completion.

What it is

Monkey Punch's Lupin III began in Futabasha's adult manga weekly Manga Action in 1967, with the original series running until 1969 and later series following. Lupin the Third is the grandson of Arsène Lupin, the gentleman thief of Maurice Leblanc's novels. He steals for the challenge as much as the money, accompanied by the marksman Daisuke Jigen and the samurai Goemon Ishikawa, betrayed again and again by the thief Fujiko Mine, and pursued across the world by Inspector Kōichi Zenigata.

How it works

Each story is a caper: a target, a plan, a disguise, a double-cross and an escape. Lupin is a master of disguise and his plans are always one step ahead of the reader. The original manga is much darker and more sexual than the later anime, with a cynical, violent Lupin, and it was aimed at adult readers.

The style

Monkey Punch drew in a loose, angular style influenced by American magazine cartoonists, which looked unlike anything else in Japanese manga at the time. Its speed and wit carried over into the characters' famous silhouettes: Lupin's thin legs and jacket, Jigen's hat over his eyes, Goemon's sword.

Why it matters

The anime adaptations, beginning in 1971, made the characters national icons. Hayao Miyazaki's first feature film, The Castle of Cagliostro (1979), is a Lupin story. Because the Lupin name was protected by copyright outside Japan, some early overseas releases renamed him, but today he is one of the most recognisable figures in Japanese popular culture.

title: Doraemon
synopsis: A robot cat from the 22nd century arrives to help a hopeless schoolboy, armed with a pocket of futuristic gadgets that always solve the problem and then cause a bigger one. Read from the structure, as a 4.
body:
4Four — foundation. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Fujiko F. Fujio's Doraemon began in 1969 in several of Shogakukan's monthly magazines for children, each aimed at a different school year, and later in CoroCoro Comic. It ran until its creator's death in 1996, and the main series was collected in 45 volumes. Nobita Nobi is a lazy, unlucky boy who fails at school and sport. His descendant in the 22nd century sends back Doraemon, a blue robot cat, to improve Nobita's future.

How it works

Almost every story follows a pattern. Nobita is bullied by the big Gian or the rich Suneo, or wants to impress Shizuka, and begs Doraemon for help. Doraemon pulls a gadget from his four-dimensional pocket: the door that opens anywhere, the bamboo copter, the time machine in Nobita's desk drawer. Nobita misuses it, and the result is a comic disaster that also carries a small lesson.

The heart

The gadgets are inventive, but the friendship between Doraemon and Nobita is what readers remember. Doraemon is a flawed, emotional friend, afraid of mice and devoted to the sweet pastry dorayaki. The series is gentle about Nobita's failures and patient with his growth.

Why it matters

It is one of the most popular children's manga ever, and its anime, broadcast since 1979, has made Doraemon a national symbol of Japan and a familiar character across Asia. In 2008 Japan named him an anime ambassador. The Fujiko F. Fujio Museum opened in Kawasaki in 2011.

title: Rurouni Kenshin
synopsis: A legendary assassin of the Meiji Restoration wanders Japan with a reverse-bladed sword, sworn never to kill again. Read from the inquiry, as a 7.
body:
7Seven — inquiry. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Nobuhiro Watsuki's Rurouni Kenshin ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1994 to 1999 and was collected in 28 volumes. In 1878, ten years into the Meiji era, Japan is modernising fast. Himura Kenshin, a small, cheerful wanderer, was once the Hitokiri Battōsai, the most feared assassin of the wars that brought down the shogunate. He now carries a sakabatō, a sword with its edge on the inner side, so that he can fight without killing.

How it works

Kenshin settles at a struggling swordsmanship school run by Kaoru Kamiya, and gathers a found family: the street fighter Sanosuke, the orphan Yahiko and the doctor Megumi. The battles are classic shōnen tournaments of named techniques, but the enemies are often men left behind by the new Japan, and each fight is also an argument about violence, atonement and whether the past can be redeemed.

The Kyoto arc

The series is best remembered for its long middle arc, in which Kenshin faces Shishio Makoto, his successor as government assassin, who was betrayed, burned and left for dead and now plans to seize the country. It tests Kenshin's vow more than any other story, and the final arc then confronts the guilt of his own past directly.

Why it matters

It brought historical drama to a mass shōnen audience, and its 1996 anime, shown in some countries as Samurai X, was hugely popular abroad. Live-action films starring Takeru Satoh (2012–2021) were major hits. Watsuki returned to the story with a sequel, the Hokkaido arc, in 2017.

title: Saint Seiya
synopsis: Teenage warriors in armour shaped like the constellations fight to protect the reincarnated goddess Athena. The title reduces to 5 — the turn.
body:
5Five — change. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Masami Kurumada's Saint Seiya ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1986 to 1990 and was collected in 28 volumes. Saints are warriors who serve Athena, the Greek goddess of war, reborn in every age to protect the Earth. Each wears a Cloth, armour based on one of the constellations. Seiya, the Pegasus Saint, and his fellow Bronze Saints, the lowest rank, discover that Athena has been reborn as a young woman, Saori Kido, and that the Sanctuary meant to serve her is plotting against her.

How it works

The Sanctuary arc is a gauntlet: to save Athena, the Bronze Saints must fight their way through twelve temples, one for each sign of the zodiac, each guarded by a Gold Saint far stronger than they are. The structure became famous. The Bronze Saints win by burning their cosmo, the universe inside each of them, beyond their limits, and by refusing to abandon one another.

The style

Kurumada had already drawn a boxing manga, and his fights are built from named attacks, shouted as they are thrown, and from heroes knocked down again and again who keep getting up. The Cloths, with their elaborate designs, were also sold as toys, which helped the series' popularity.

Why it matters

It was a major hit in Japan and an even bigger one in parts of Europe and Latin America, where the anime aired as Les Chevaliers du Zodiaque in France and Os Cavaleiros do Zodíaco in Brazil. Its model of ranked warriors, armour and a gauntlet of guardians influenced many later battle manga.

title: Great Teacher Onizuka
synopsis: A 22-year-old former biker gang leader becomes a teacher, and takes on the class that has driven every teacher before him out of the school. 91 in the letters, reducing to 1.

1The letters of this title total 91, a 1 — the number of beginnings, leadership, and the will to act alone.

What it is

Tōru Fujisawa's Great Teacher Onizuka, usually called GTO, ran in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 1997 to 2002 and was collected in 25 volumes. Eikichi Onizuka is 22, a former leader of a biker gang with dyed hair and few qualifications, who decides to become a teacher, at first for embarrassing reasons. He is given a class at a private middle school whose students have humiliated and broken the teachers before him.

How it works

Each arc centres on a student: one who has been bullied, one whose parents ignore her, one who plans to destroy him. Onizuka solves their problems in outrageous ways, by smashing walls, jumping off buildings and ignoring every rule, but always by taking the students' side when no other adult will. The school administration, which cares about reputation more than children, is the real villain.

The tone

The series swings between crude comedy and serious subjects, including suicide, abuse and family breakdown. Onizuka's stupidity is part of the joke, but his willingness to put himself in danger for his students is the point.

Why it matters

It is a sequel to Fujisawa's delinquent manga Shonan Junai Gumi, and it carried that genre into the school drama. It won the Kodansha Manga Award, and its 1998 television drama and 1999 anime were both big successes. Its fantasy of a teacher who actually listens still resonates with readers.

title: Initial D
synopsis: A quiet teenager who delivers tofu down a mountain road every night turns out to be the best street racer in the region. The title reduces to 6 — the care.
body:
6Six — responsibility. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Shūichi Shigeno's Initial D ran in Kodansha's Weekly Young Magazine from 1995 to 2013 and was collected in 48 volumes. Takumi Fujiwara is an unremarkable high-school student in Gunma Prefecture. Every morning before dawn he drives his father's tofu delivery car, an old Toyota AE86, down the winding road of Mount Akina. Without realising it, he has become an extraordinary driver, and the local street racers soon want to know who is behind the wheel.

How it works

The series is a sequence of races on real-feeling mountain passes, each against a rival with a different car and philosophy. Shigeno explains the techniques, from drifting to braking points and tyre wear, in detail, and the drama comes from how a slower, older car can win through skill and knowledge of the road. Takumi's father Bunta, a former racer, teaches him almost without speaking.

The style

Shigeno's characters are simply drawn, but the cars are drawn with precise realism, and the races use speed lines, close-ups and the view from the driver's seat to create motion on a still page.

Why it matters

It is the definitive street-racing manga. Its anime, with its soundtrack of Eurobeat music, became a cult hit, and it raised the price of the AE86 among real enthusiasts. Shigeno continued its world in MF Ghost.

title: Ashita no Joe
synopsis: A drifter from the slums of Tokyo becomes a boxer and fights his way towards a world title, at a cost that consumes him. Read from the closing, as a 9.
body:
9A 9 by its title: humanitarian & sage, and therefore the closing.

What it is

Ashita no Joe, written by Ikki Kajiwara under the pen name Asao Takamori and drawn by Tetsuya Chiba, ran in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 1968 to 1973 and was collected in 20 volumes. Joe Yabuki is a reckless, defiant young drifter who turns up in a Tokyo slum. A washed-up boxing trainer, Danpei Tange, sees his talent, and after Joe is sent to a reformatory he discovers boxing there through his rival, Tōru Rikiishi.

How it works

The story follows Joe's career from the slums to a world title fight, but it is not a simple rise. Each opponent leaves a mark on him, and the series is honest about the damage boxing does to the body and mind. Joe fights not for money or glory, but because the ring is the only place where he feels fully alive.

Rikiishi

Rikiishi starves himself to drop weight classes so that he can fight Joe, wins, and dies soon after the bout. The death shocked readers so deeply that a real funeral was held for the character in 1970. The ending, in which Joe sits in his corner, smiling, "burned out to white ash", is one of the most famous images in manga.

Why it matters

It was read by students and adults as much as by children, and became a symbol of its era: in 1970, the hijackers of a Japanese airliner declared, "We are Ashita no Joe." With Kajiwara's other work it defined the spokon sports story, and Chiba's art set a standard for drawing fighters and the people around them.

title: Hellsing
synopsis: A British secret organisation hunts monsters with a monster of its own: an ancient and nearly unstoppable vampire. Filed under 5, the turn.
body:

What it is

Kōta Hirano's Hellsing ran in Shōnen Gahōsha's Young King OURs from 1997 to 2008 and was collected in 10 volumes. The Hellsing Organisation, led by Sir Integra Hellsing, protects Britain from vampires and other supernatural threats. Its greatest weapon is Alucard, a vampire of terrifying power bound to serve the Hellsing family. In the first chapter he turns a young police officer, Seras Victoria, into a vampire, and she becomes his reluctant apprentice.

How it works

The early chapters are monster-hunting episodes, but the series soon becomes a three-way war between Hellsing, the Vatican's fanatical Section XIII Iscariot, led by the priest Alexander Anderson, and Millennium, a battalion of surviving Nazi soldiers turned into artificial vampires, who invade London. The war is drawn at enormous scale and with extreme violence.

The style

Hirano draws in heavy blacks, sharp angles and exaggerated, grinning faces, and his pages are full of speeches, poses and dramatic close-ups. The tone is over the top on purpose, mixing horror, action and grim comedy. Under it is a question about what it means to be human, which Alucard asks of every opponent.

Why it matters

It is a cult classic of seinen action and one of the best-known vampire manga. Its anime adaptations, especially the faithful Hellsing Ultimate (2006–2012), made it famous worldwide. Hirano's next series, Drifters, began in 2009.

title: Neon Genesis Evangelion
altTitles: 新世紀エヴァンゲリオン
synopsis: The character designer of the anime retells it in manga: a withdrawn boy is made to pilot a giant machine against mysterious beings attacking the city. Filed under 5, the turn.
body:
5The letters of this title total 104, a 5 — the number of freedom, disruption, and restless movement.

What it is

Yoshiyuki Sadamoto's manga of Neon Genesis Evangelion began in Kadokawa's Monthly Shōnen Ace in 1994, shortly before the anime series it accompanies first aired, moved to Young Ace and finished in 2013, collected in 14 volumes. Sadamoto was the anime's character designer. In 2015, fifteen years after a catastrophe that killed half of humanity, fourteen-year-old Shinji Ikari is summoned by his estranged father to Tokyo-3 and ordered to pilot the giant Evangelion Unit-01 against beings called Angels.

How it works

The manga follows the anime's story, but not always its scenes. Sadamoto gives more space to the characters' inner lives and rewrites some relationships: his Shinji is more sullen and angry, and the mysterious Kaworu Nagisa is introduced differently. The giant robot battles are there, but the centre is a boy who does not want to fight and adults who use him.

Its pace

Because Sadamoto worked on the anime and its later films at the same time, the manga appeared slowly, with long breaks, across nearly two decades. Readers who began it as teenagers finished it as adults.

Why it matters

The anime transformed the mecha genre into psychological drama, and Sadamoto's manga is its most personal retelling, by the artist who gave its characters their faces. It is often recommended as a different way into the story for viewers who know the series.

title: Kochikame
altTitles: こちら葛飾区亀有公園前派出所
synopsis: A greedy, lazy and endlessly inventive Tokyo police officer gets into a new scheme every week, for forty years without a break. 40 in the letters, reducing to 4.

4Reduced, this title gives 4. It sits on The Structure with the rest of a structure.

What it is

Osamu Akimoto's Kochikame, short for a title meaning "This is the police box in front of Kameari Park in Katsushika Ward", ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1976 to 2016. It appeared in every issue for forty years without a single break and was collected in 200 volumes. Kankichi Ryōtsu is a middle-aged police officer in a working-class district of Tokyo: lazy, greedy, loud and brilliant at anything that might make him money.

How it works

Almost every chapter is self-contained. Ryōtsu discovers a new hobby, gadget or business, throws himself into it with absurd energy, makes a fortune and loses it, usually ending in trouble with his chief. Around him are his wealthy and polite colleagues, Reiko and Nakagawa, whose families can buy anything, and a large cast of neighbours.

A record of its time

Because Ryōtsu chased every trend, the series became an accidental chronicle of four decades of Japanese life: video games, model kits, computers, the stock market, mobile phones. Akimoto researched each subject in detail, and readers learned real facts along with the jokes. The downtown setting also preserved a picture of old Tokyo neighbourhoods as they changed.

Why it matters

It is the longest uninterrupted run in Jump's history. When it ended, it held the Guinness record for the most volumes of a single manga series. Its anime ran from 1996 to 2004, and Ryōtsu's statue stands near Kameari Station.

title: Golgo 13
synopsis: The world's most expensive assassin takes contracts from governments, corporations and criminals, never speaks more than he must, and never misses. Read from the signal, as an 11.
body:
11An 11 by its title: visionary (master 11), and therefore the signal.

What it is

Takao Saito's Golgo 13 began in Shogakukan's Big Comic in 1968 and is still running. Its hero, known as Duke Tōgō or Golgo 13, is a sniper of superhuman skill whose real name, nationality and past are unknown. He accepts contracts from anyone who can pay his fee and keeps to strict rules: he never lets anyone stand behind him, and he never fails.

How it works

Each story is a self-contained thriller. A client explains a problem, often tied to real politics, wars, finance or technology, and Golgo solves it with a single, impossible shot. He says very little, and the stories are told mostly through the people around him. The series became a way to explore world events, from the Cold War to modern terrorism.

The studio system

Saito ran his work like a film production. His studio divided the work among scriptwriters, researchers and artists, each with a role, and he directed the result. This system let the series appear reliably for decades, and it continued after Saito's death in 2021, as he had wished.

Why it matters

It is one of the defining works of gekiga, the realistic manga for adults. In 2021 it was recognised by Guinness World Records for the most volumes published of a single manga series. Golgo's stern face and bushy eyebrows are known across Japan.

title: Yu-Gi-Oh!
synopsis: A shy boy solves an ancient puzzle and gains a second self, the spirit of a pharaoh who settles every challenge with a game. Read from the structure, as a 4.
body:
4A 4 by its title: builder & organizer, and therefore the structure.

What it is

Kazuki Takahashi's Yu-Gi-Oh! ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1996 to 2004 and was collected in 38 volumes. Yugi Mutō is a timid high-school student who loves games. He completes the Millennium Puzzle, an Egyptian artefact, and it awakens a spirit within him: a bold, confident self who challenges wrongdoers to games with terrible penalties.

How it works

At first each chapter featured a different game, from dice to video games. One of them, a card game called Magic & Wizards, later Duel Monsters, proved so popular that the series came to centre on it. Yugi and his friends face the arrogant genius Seto Kaiba and a series of villains in tournaments, and the spirit within Yugi is revealed as a pharaoh whose lost memories lie in ancient Egypt.

The game

Takahashi designed the cards and rules as he went, and the duels became tense battles of strategy and bluff. In 1999 Konami released a real trading card game based on the manga, which became one of the best-selling card games in the world.

Why it matters

It is one of the most successful examples of the media mix, in which a manga, anime, card game and video games feed one another. Its anime and many sequels made it a worldwide phenomenon, and the card game is still played competitively today.

title: Kimi ni Todoke
synopsis: A sweet, shy girl whom classmates nickname after a horror-film ghost slowly makes friends and falls in love. Read from the closing, as a 9.

What it is

Karuho Shiina's Kimi ni Todoke ran in Shueisha's Bessatsu Margaret from 2005 to 2017 and was collected in 30 volumes. Sawako Kuronuma is a kind, earnest high-school girl, but her long black hair and awkwardness have earned her the nickname Sadako, after the ghost in Ring. Classmates believe rumours that she can curse people. Only the popular, friendly Shōta Kazehaya treats her normally.

How it works

The story is slow and gentle. Sawako learns to talk to people, makes her first real friends, Ayane and Chizuru, and gradually realises what she feels for Kazehaya. Misunderstandings, school festivals and small steps forward take many chapters, and that patience is the point: each change in Sawako's life is felt fully.

Shiina writes with warmth and humour, and her characters are kind even when they misunderstand one another. The series is as much about friendship as romance, and about how being seen by others can change who you are.

It is one of the best-loved shōjo romances of its era, and won the Kodansha Manga Award for shōjo. Its anime adaptation, from 2009, and later live-action versions brought it a wide audience.

What it is

Bisco Hatori's Ouran High School Host Club ran in Hakusensha's LaLa from 2002 to 2010 and was collected in 18 volumes. Haruhi Fujioka is a practical, unflappable scholarship student at Ouran Academy, a school for the children of the very rich. Looking for a quiet place to study, she stumbles into the Host Club, where six handsome boys entertain the school's girls, and breaks a vase worth eight million yen.

How it works

With her short hair and plain clothes, the club takes Haruhi for a boy, and she agrees to work as a host to pay off the debt. Most chapters are comic episodes: themed parties, beach trips, rivalries. The club's president, the dramatic and romantic Tamaki, the cool Kyōya, the mischievous twins Hikaru and Kaoru and the others each have their own story.

The parody

The series gently mocks shōjo conventions: the handsome-boy types, the rich-school fantasy and the dramatic gestures. Haruhi, who cares nothing for money or appearances, sees through all of it, and her indifference to whether she is seen as a boy or a girl is part of the joke and part of her appeal.

Why it matters

Its 2006 anime by Studio Bones was popular internationally, and it remains one of the best-known shōjo comedies. It showed how a series could love a genre while making fun of it.

title: Nodame Cantabile
synopsis: A perfectionist music student who dreams of conducting falls in with a messy, brilliant pianist who plays entirely by ear. Filed under 11, the signal.
body:
11Title sums to 56 and reduces to 11 — The Signal, where the reference files a signal received early.

What it is

Tomoko Ninomiya's Nodame Cantabile ran in Kodansha's Kiss from 2001 to 2010 and was collected in 25 volumes. Shinichi Chiaki is a gifted, arrogant music student who wants to become a conductor, but a fear of flying keeps him stuck in Japan. Megumi Noda, known as Nodame, is his neighbour: chaotic and childlike, lives in a filthy flat, and is a pianist of extraordinary instinct who cannot read a score properly.

How it works

The first half is set at a music college in Tokyo, where Chiaki forms an orchestra of misfits and Nodame struggles to take her own talent seriously. The second half moves to Paris, where both must compete in a much larger world. The comedy is broad, but the music is treated with respect: real pieces are performed, rehearsed and argued over, and the stories explain what the musicians are trying to achieve.

The relationship

Chiaki and Nodame are a comic mismatch, and their romance grows slowly. The deeper story is about each of them learning from the other: Chiaki to feel, Nodame to work.

Why it matters

It won the Kodansha Manga Award for shōjo, and its 2006 television drama was so successful that it drew new audiences to classical music in Japan. It is one of the best-known music manga and a model for josei series that combine comedy and professional ambition.

title: Usagi Drop
synopsis: A single office worker in his thirties takes in his late grandfather's six-year-old daughter, and learns how to raise a child. Read from the signal, as an 11.
body:
11Eleven — vision. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Yumi Unita's Usagi Drop ran in Shodensha's Feel Young from 2005 to 2011. Daikichi, a thirty-year-old single office worker, attends his grandfather's funeral and discovers that the old man left behind a six-year-old daughter, Rin. When the relatives refuse to take her in, Daikichi impulsively decides to raise her himself.

How it works

The first half is a gentle, detailed story of learning to be a parent: finding a nursery, changing jobs to work fewer hours, coping with illnesses and school events, and meeting other single parents. Daikichi has no idea what he is doing, and the series takes his small discoveries seriously. Rin is drawn as a real child, quiet, stubborn and observant.

The time skip

The second half jumps ten years, to Rin as a teenager, and turns to her questions about her mother, her future and her feelings. Its ending divided readers, and many who love the first half recommend reading it with that in mind.

Why it matters

It is a celebrated josei manga about care and family, and one of the few to centre on a man learning to parent alone. Its 2011 anime and live-action film both adapted only the first half.

title: Hajime no Ippo
synopsis: A bullied boy from a fishing-boat family discovers boxing and begins a long climb through the professional ranks. Read from the turn, as a 5.
body:
5A 5 by its title: freedom seeker, and therefore the turn.

What it is

George Morikawa's Hajime no Ippo has run in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine since 1989 and passed 140 volumes. Ippo Makunouchi is a shy high-school student who helps his mother run a fishing-boat business and is bullied at school. A boxer, Mamoru Takamura, rescues him and brings him to the Kamogawa Gym, where Ippo discovers that he wants to know what it means to be strong.

How it works

The series follows Ippo's professional career fight by fight, with long, detailed bouts and the training between them. Morikawa explains real boxing techniques, and Ippo develops his own, such as the weaving Dempsey Roll. His opponents are given full stories, and many become friends. Takamura, a crude and hilarious genius, and the gym's elderly coach, Kamogawa, are as important as Ippo.

The style

Morikawa's fights are some of the most kinetic in manga, with punches shown in sequence and their impact felt in faces and bodies. The comedy at the gym balances the violence of the ring.

Why it matters

It won the Kodansha Manga Award in 1991 and is the definitive boxing manga of its era. Its anime, from 2000, is highly regarded, and Morikawa has spoken about wanting to encourage interest in real boxing.

title: Sazae-san
synopsis: A cheerful, scatterbrained young housewife and her extended family live through the ordinary comedy of postwar Japan, four panels at a time. Read from the turn, as a 5.
body:
5A 5 by its title: freedom seeker, and therefore the turn.

What it is

Machiko Hasegawa's Sazae-san began in 1946 in a Fukuoka newspaper, moved to the national Asahi Shimbun in 1949, and ran there until 1974. It is a yonkoma, a four-panel strip. Sazae is a cheerful, careless and energetic young woman who lives with her husband Masuo, their son Tarao, her parents and her younger brother and sister, Katsuo and Wakame.

How it works

Each strip is a small domestic joke: a mistake, a misunderstanding, a family argument or a comment on the news. Because it ran in a daily newspaper for decades, it followed the changes in postwar Japanese life, from food shortages to television and household appliances, through the eyes of an ordinary family.

Sazae

Sazae is no meek housewife. She is loud, opinionated and often ridiculous, and the strip enjoys her independence. Hasegawa also wrote about women's lives with sharp humour in her other strips.

Why it matters

It is one of the most beloved works in Japanese popular culture. Its anime, broadcast weekly on Sunday evenings since 1969, holds the Guinness World Record as the longest-running animated television series. The Hasegawa Machiko Art Museum in Tokyo is dedicated to her work.

title: Tokyo Ghoul
altTitles: 東京喰種トーキョーグール
synopsis: A shy student becomes half ghoul, one of the hidden flesh-eaters living in Tokyo, and must survive between two worlds that want him dead. 50 in the letters, reducing to 5.

What it is

Sui Ishida's Tokyo Ghoul ran in Shueisha's Weekly Young Jump from 2011 to 2014 and was collected in 14 volumes, followed by the sequel Tokyo Ghoul:re (2014–2018). Ghouls look human but can only survive by eating human flesh, and they live hidden in Tokyo. Ken Kaneki, a shy university student who loves books, is attacked on a date by a ghoul. After an accident, her organs are transplanted into him, and he wakes up half ghoul.

How it works

Kaneki finds refuge at Anteiku, a coffee shop run by ghouls who try to live peacefully, and learns that ghouls are as varied as humans: some cruel, some desperate, some kind. Against them are the investigators of the CCG, who hunt ghouls as monsters. The story asks who is really monstrous, and makes both sides sympathetic.

The transformation

Kaneki changes violently over the series. After he is captured and tortured, he becomes harder and more dangerous, and his white hair marks the change. Ishida's art, which grows looser and more experimental over time, reflects his unstable mind.

Why it matters

It was one of the biggest seinen hits of the 2010s, and its 2014 anime made it a worldwide phenomenon. Its mixture of horror, action and identity crisis influenced many later dark-fantasy series.

title: Kaiji
synopsis: A broke, aimless young man drowning in a friend's debt is offered a way out through a series of high-stakes gambles run by the very rich. 22 in the letters, with nothing left to reduce.
body:
22The letters of this title total 22 outright — the number of grand vision made concrete and built to last.

What it is

Nobuyuki Fukumoto's Kaiji began in Kodansha's Weekly Young Magazine in 1996 and has continued through a long series of sequels. Kaiji Itō is a lazy, resentful young man in Tokyo who has guaranteed a friend's loan. When the friend disappears, a loan shark offers Kaiji a chance to clear the debt in one night: by boarding a cruise ship and gambling.

How it works

Each arc is a single game, designed by the organisers to exploit desperate people: a rock-paper-scissors tournament played with cards, a walk across a narrow steel beam between skyscrapers, a card game modelled on an emperor, a citizen and a slave. The rules are explained precisely, and the drama comes from reading opponents, spotting the trick in the rules and finding the one move that might win.

The style

Fukumoto draws his characters with sharp chins and noses and fills the background with a rustling sound effect, zawa zawa, that has become his trademark. Kaiji weeps, sweats and despairs openly, and the inner monologue is long and tense. The series is as much about fear and greed as about strategy.

Why it matters

It won the Kodansha Manga Award and is a founding work of the gambling and death-game genres in manga. Its villains, wealthy men who treat the poor as entertainment, made it a lasting satire of debt and inequality. It has been adapted as an anime and as live-action films.

title: Gantz
synopsis: People who have just died wake up in a room with a black sphere, which sends them out with strange weapons to hunt aliens across Tokyo. Filed under 5, the turn.
body:
5Reduced, this title gives 5. It sits on The Turn with the rest of a turn.

What it is

Hiroya Oku's Gantz ran in Shueisha's Weekly Young Jump from 2000 to 2013 and was collected in 37 volumes. High-school student Kei Kurono and his childhood friend Masaru Katō are hit by a subway train while trying to rescue a homeless man. They wake up in an apartment with a large black sphere and a group of strangers who have also just died. The sphere, called Gantz, gives them suits and weapons and sends them out to kill aliens.

How it works

Each mission is a brutal fight against bizarre creatures, scored in points. Those who survive go home until the next summons; those who reach 100 points may be freed or bring someone back to life. The missions grow larger and deadlier, and the story eventually expands into an invasion of Earth.

The art

Oku was one of the first manga artists to build his pages with 3D computer models, especially for backgrounds and vehicles, combined with photographic detail. The result is a hyper-real, almost cinematic Tokyo, against which the violence is shocking.

Why it matters

It is one of the most influential death-game manga, and its mixture of extreme violence, sexuality and moral questions made it a cult hit. It was adapted as an anime, as two live-action films (2011) and as the CG film Gantz:O (2016).

title: Claymore
synopsis: Silver-eyed women, half human and half demon, are hired to kill the monsters that feed on people, and fight to keep from becoming monsters themselves. Filed under 11, the signal.

What it is

Norihiro Yagi's Claymore began in Shueisha's Monthly Shōnen Jump in 2001, moved to Jump SQ in 2007 and ended in 2014, collected in 27 volumes. In a medieval world, creatures called yoma devour human beings and can take human form. A mysterious Organisation creates warriors to fight them by implanting yoma flesh into young women, who are known by their silver eyes and huge swords as Claymores.

How it works

Clare is the weakest of the Organisation's 47 ranked warriors. Each warrior has a number, from No. 1, the strongest, to No. 47, and a release of her yoma power makes her stronger but risks pushing her over the edge into becoming an Awakened Being, a monster far worse than any yoma. Clare travels with Raki, a boy whose family was killed, seeking revenge for Teresa, the warrior who saved her as a child.

The world

The Organisation is a source of horror in its own right, using its warriors as tools and hiding its purpose. The story follows Clare and a group of survivors who rebel against it, and the scale grows from village hunts to wars between Awakened Beings.

Why it matters

It is a respected dark fantasy, with a rare cast made up almost entirely of women warriors. Its 2007 anime by Madhouse brought it an international audience, and its themes of transformation and identity sit alongside series such as Berserk.

title: Made in Abyss
synopsis: An orphan girl and a robot boy descend into a vast, unexplored pit full of wonders and horrors, from which no one returns unchanged. 40 in the letters, reducing to 4.
body:
4Title sums to 40 and reduces to 4 — The Structure, where the reference files a structure.

What it is

Akihito Tsukushi's Made in Abyss has run on Takeshobo's Web Comic Gamma since 2012. Beside the town of Orth lies the Abyss, an enormous pit whose depths have never been fully explored. Cave Raiders descend into it to recover relics, and are ranked by the colour of their whistles. Riko, an orphan training as a raider, finds a robot boy, Reg, who has no memory, and receives a message that may be from her mother, a legendary raider lost in the depths.

How it works

The Abyss is divided into layers, each with its own landscape and creatures. Its central rule is the Curse: anyone who climbs back up suffers effects that grow worse with depth, from nausea to loss of humanity or death. Going down is easy; coming back may be impossible. Riko and Reg descend anyway, knowing they may never return.

The contrast

Tsukushi draws the characters as rounded, childlike figures and the Abyss with detailed, beautiful landscapes, so the series looks like a gentle adventure. It is not. The children suffer terrible injuries and encounter cruelty, and the contrast between innocence and violence is deliberate, if hard for some readers to bear.

Why it matters

Its worldbuilding, with its layers, relics and curse, is among the most admired in recent manga. Its 2017 anime by Kinema Citrus was a major success, praised especially for its music and art, and brought the series a wide international readership.

title: Cells at Work!
synopsis: The cells of the human body are drawn as workers: a lost red blood cell delivers oxygen while white blood cells fight off germs. The title reduces to 4 — the structure.
body:
4A 4 by its title: builder & organizer, and therefore the structure.

What it is

Akane Shimizu's Cells at Work! ran in Kodansha's Monthly Shōnen Sirius from 2015 to 2021 and was collected in 6 volumes. Inside a human body, the cells are workers in a busy city. A clumsy red blood cell, numbered AE3803, keeps getting lost while delivering oxygen, and a white blood cell, U-1146, keeps rescuing her from invading bacteria.

How it works

Each chapter is about a real process in the body: a cut, a cold, an allergy, heatstroke, a vaccine, cancer. The cells are characters with jobs, so platelets are small children who seal wounds, killer T cells are tough soldiers and macrophages are elegant ladies who are also ferocious fighters. Captions explain the real biology behind each scene.

Why it works

The series is funny and exciting, but it is also accurate enough that teachers and doctors have recommended it. It turns the abstractions of biology into a story with characters, and its explanations stay with readers because they are attached to a scene.

Why it matters

It is one of the most successful educational manga of recent years. Its 2018 anime, a live-action film (2024) and many spin-offs, including the darker Cells at Work! Code Black, about the body of an unhealthy adult, have spread it widely.

title: Laid-Back Camp
synopsis: A girl who likes to camp alone in winter meets a cheerful newcomer, and both discover the pleasures of camping in the countryside around Mount Fuji. Filed under 4, the structure.
body:
4Reduced, this title gives 4. It sits on The Structure with the rest of a structure.

What it is

Afro's Laid-Back Camp has run in Houbunsha's Manga Time Kirara Forward since 2015. Rin Shima is a quiet high-school girl in Yamanashi Prefecture who loves to camp alone, especially in the off-season when campsites are empty. At a lakeside campsite she meets Nadeshiko Kagamihara, an energetic girl who has just moved to the area and has fallen asleep on the way to see Mount Fuji.

How it works

Nadeshiko joins her school's tiny Outdoor Activities Club and gradually draws Rin into group trips, although Rin still values her solo camps. Each chapter covers a trip: choosing a site, setting up a tent, cooking, keeping warm, and looking at the view. There is almost no conflict, and the pleasure lies in the details and the company.

The practical side

The series is full of real information, about equipment, campsite booking, cooking on a burner and staying warm in winter, and its locations are real places around Mount Fuji and the Fuji Five Lakes. Readers learn how to camp while watching the characters do it.

Its 2018 anime was widely credited with a boom in camping among young people in Japan and with drawing visitors to the locations it shows. It is one of the best examples of a manga that makes a hobby irresistible, and of the gentle, comforting slice-of-life that Kirara magazines publish.

title: Nichijou
synopsis: Three schoolgirls, a robot girl, an eight-year-old professor and a talking cat live a daily life in which absolutely anything can happen. The title reduces to 8 — the ledger.
body:
8An 8 by its title: visionary & achiever, and therefore the ledger.

What it is

Keiichi Arawi's Nichijou, meaning "everyday life", began in Kadokawa's Monthly Shōnen Ace in 2006. It paused in 2015 and resumed in 2021. Yūko, Mio and Mai are high-school friends in a quiet town. Nearby lives Nano, a robot girl with a large wind-up key in her back, who wants to be ordinary, built by the Professor, a genius who is eight years old, and their cat Sakamoto, who can talk thanks to a scarf the Professor made.

How it works

The series is a collection of short sketches, some only a page or two long. Most begin with something very ordinary, such as forgetting your homework, buying a snack or trying to make a joke, and escalate into absurd catastrophe: a fight that turns into a martial-arts epic, a fall drawn as a cosmic event. Others are deadpan and almost nothing happens.

The humour

Arawi's comedy depends on timing, scale and contrast. A tiny misunderstanding is treated as a disaster, and a real disaster is shrugged off. His clean, simple drawing and large empty spaces make the explosions of absurdity land harder.

Why it matters

Its 2011 anime by Kyoto Animation, famous for its inventive animation of the gags, made it a cult classic. It is one of the purest examples of manga absurdist comedy, and many fans consider it one of the funniest manga ever made.

What it is

Taiyō Matsumoto's Tekkonkinkreet ran in Shogakukan's Big Comic Spirits from 1993 to 1994 and was collected in 3 volumes. Its title is a child's mispronunciation of "reinforced concrete". In Treasure Town, a crowded, crumbling city, two orphans known as the Cats rule the streets: Kuro, Black, a fierce, street-smart fighter, and Shiro, White, a dreamy, childlike boy who seems to live in another world.

How it works

Yakuza, a mysterious developer who wants to replace the old town with a theme park, and his inhuman assassins threaten the boys' home. As the city changes, Kuro's violence grows and the bond between the two is tested. The story is about the balance between them: each holds what the other lacks.

The art

Matsumoto draws Treasure Town with wobbling perspective, bent buildings and dense, chaotic detail, influenced by European comics as much as by manga. The boys leap between rooftops as if gravity hardly applies, and the city feels alive.

Why it matters

It is one of the key works of alternative manga and of Matsumoto's career. Its 2006 animated film, directed by Michael Arias at Studio 4°C, was celebrated for bringing his distinctive look to the screen.

title: The Heart of Thomas
synopsis: At a German boarding school, a boy's death leaves a letter of love addressed to the classmate who rejected him, and changes everyone it touches. Read from the signal, as an 11.
body:
11An 11 by its title: visionary (master 11), and therefore the signal.

What it is

Moto Hagio's The Heart of Thomas was serialised in Shogakukan's Weekly Shōjo Comic in 1974. At a boys' boarding school in Germany, a gentle student, Thomas Werner, falls to his death from a bridge. Before he died, he sent a letter to Juli, an older student who had rejected him. Soon after, a new boy, Erich, arrives at the school, looking almost exactly like Thomas.

How it works

The story follows Juli, a brilliant, cold student who is hiding a painful secret, and the boys around him, as they try to understand Thomas's death. It is less a mystery than a study of guilt, love and forgiveness. Thomas's sacrifice, it gradually emerges, was meant as a gift.

Its place in history

It is one of the founding works of shōnen-ai, stories of love between boys written for girls, and one of the key works of the Year 24 Group of women artists who transformed shōjo manga in the 1970s. Its European setting, religious themes and psychological depth were new to girls' magazines.

Why it matters

It is a classic of shōjo manga and one of Hagio's most celebrated works. Its influence can be traced through decades of later manga about boarding schools, longing and the inner lives of young people.

title: Tomie
synopsis: A beautiful girl drives the men around her to madness and murder, and every time she is killed, she comes back. 26 in the letters, reducing to 8.
body:
8The letters of this title total 26, an 8 — the number of money, authority, and the machinery of ambition.

What it is

Tomie was Junji Ito's first published work. It won an honourable mention in the Kazuo Umezu Prize in 1987 and appeared in Asahi Sonorama's horror magazine Monthly Halloween, and Ito returned to it in stories published until 2000. Tomie Kawakami is a beautiful, manipulative schoolgirl. In the first story, her classmates and teacher murder her and dismember her body. The next day she walks into class.

How it works

The stories are loosely connected episodes. Tomie attracts men, who become obsessed with her and eventually try to kill her. She cannot be destroyed: every piece of her body, even a drop of blood, can grow into a new Tomie, and the new Tomies hate one another. Each story shows a different person, family or town falling apart around her.

The horror

Tomie is less a monster than a force that brings out jealousy, desire and violence in others. Ito draws her as calm and perfect, while the people around her become grotesque. The recurring image of a body regrowing from a fragment is one of his most disturbing.

Why it matters

It launched the career of the most celebrated horror artist in manga and established the themes of obsession and bodily horror that run through his work. It has been adapted into a long series of films beginning in 1999.

title: Bocchi the Rock!
synopsis: A painfully shy girl who has spent years practising guitar alone in her room is pulled into a real band, and has to face an audience. 66 in the letters, reducing to 3.

What it is

Aki Hamaji's Bocchi the Rock! has run in Houbunsha's four-panel magazine Manga Time Kirara Max since 2017. Hitori Gotō is so socially anxious that she can barely speak to anyone. She took up the guitar in middle school, hoping a band would make her popular, and practised for hours every day, but never made a single friend to play with. Online, under the name guitarhero, she posts cover videos that many people watch. In person, she is "Bocchi", a word for someone who is always alone.

How it works

Nijika Ijichi, a cheerful drummer, drags Hitori into her band, Kessoku Band, at a small live house in Shimokitazawa, Tokyo. With the cool, broke bassist Ryō Yamada and the outgoing singer Ikuyo Kita, Hitori begins to rehearse, write lyrics, take part-time jobs and play live. Each step is agony for her, and the comedy comes from her extravagant panic.

The comedy

Hitori's anxiety is drawn with wild exaggeration: she melts, falls to pieces, turns into a block of stone or imagines whole futures of humiliation. The jokes are affectionate rather than cruel, and many readers recognise themselves in her fears. Beneath them is a story of real progress, as she slowly finds people who accept her.

Why it matters

Its 2022 anime by CloverWorks was a major hit, admired for its inventive animation and its music, and the band's album sold strongly in Japan. It brought new attention to the four-panel Kirara magazines and to stories about social anxiety.

title: K-On!
synopsis: Four high-school girls revive their school's light music club, and spend more time drinking tea and eating cake than practising. The title reduces to 4 — the structure.
body:
4Filed under 4. The Structure takes a structure, and this entry is frames one.

What it is

kakifly's K-On! began in Houbunsha's Manga Time Kirara in 2007. Its main story ended in 2010, and two follow-up series, about the characters at university and the younger members left at school, ran until 2012. Its title is short for keiongaku, "light music", the Japanese term for pop and rock. Ritsu Tainaka and Mio Akiyama join their high school's light music club to save it from closure, along with the wealthy, kind Tsumugi Kotobuki and Yui Hirasawa, who has never played an instrument.

How it works

The series is a four-panel comedy. Yui buys a guitar, learns to play surprisingly fast and forgets everything else; the club practises a little and spends most of its time over tea and cake in the clubroom. A serious younger student, Azusa Nakano, joins and despairs at their laziness, then comes to love them. Each season brings school festivals, trips and performances.

The mood

There is almost no conflict. The pleasure is in friendship, small jokes and the feeling of a school year passing. When the older members graduate, the series lets them feel the end of something precious.

Why it matters

Its 2009 anime by Kyoto Animation was a phenomenon, and it was widely reported to have boosted sales of the guitars and other instruments its characters play. It became the defining example of the gentle club comedies known as "cute girls doing cute things".

title: Oshi no Ko
synopsis: A doctor is murdered and reborn as the son of the idol he adored, and grows up inside the entertainment industry hunting the man responsible for her death. Filed under 7, the inquiry.
body:
7The letters of this title total 43, a 7 — the number of analysis, secrecy, and the search for truth.

What it is

Oshi no Ko, written by Aka Akasaka and drawn by Mengo Yokoyari, ran in Shueisha's Weekly Young Jump from 2020 to 2024 and was collected in 16 volumes. Gorō Amamiya, a rural doctor, is a devoted fan of the teenage idol Ai Hoshino. When she secretly comes to his hospital to give birth to twins, he is murdered by a stalker, and wakes up reborn as one of her children, Aquamarine, with his memories intact. His twin sister Ruby, he later learns, is also reborn.

How it works

Ai is murdered while the twins are still small. Aqua grows up determined to find the man who arranged it, and enters the entertainment world to do so: acting, reality television and stage plays. Ruby pursues her mother's dream of becoming an idol. The revenge plot runs through a detailed, often critical portrait of how the Japanese entertainment industry works.

The industry

Akasaka uses each arc to show a different part of the business: a reality show that drives a performer to despair, a manga adaptation whose author and screenwriter clash, the training and exploitation of idols. The series became known for treating these topics seriously, and its title refers to an oshi, the performer a fan supports above all others.

Why it matters

Its 2023 anime by Doga Kobo was a huge hit, and its opening song, "Idol" by YOASOBI, topped international charts. Its mixture of reincarnation, mystery and showbusiness drama made it one of the most discussed manga of its time.

title: Dandadan
synopsis: A girl who believes in ghosts and a boy who believes in aliens each try to prove the other wrong, and discover that both exist. Read from the inquiry, as a 7.

7Filed under 7. The Inquiry takes an open question, and this entry is examines one.

What it is

Yukinobu Tatsu's Dandadan has run on Shueisha's Shōnen Jump+ since 2021. Momo Ayase, a high-school girl from a family of spirit mediums, believes in ghosts but not aliens. Ken Takakura, a nerdy boy she nicknames Okarun, believes in aliens but not ghosts. To settle the argument, she visits a site haunted by UFOs, and he visits a haunted tunnel. Both are right.

How it works

Momo is abducted by aliens and discovers psychic powers; Okarun is possessed by a malevolent spirit, the Turbo Granny, who steals his most precious possession. The two must work together to recover it, and the series becomes a breakneck mixture of ghost story, alien invasion, martial arts and romantic comedy, with new monsters drawn from Japanese urban legends and UFO lore.

The style

Tatsu, who previously worked as an assistant to Tatsuki Fujimoto, draws dense, kinetic action and grotesque creatures, and switches abruptly between gross-out comedy, horror and sincere emotion. Many readers come for the fights and stay for Momo and Okarun's awkward romance.

It became one of the flagship series of Jump+, showing how far web serialisation now shapes mainstream manga. Its 2024 anime by Science SARU was a major international success.

title: Sakamoto Days
synopsis: The greatest hitman of his age retires for love, runs a corner shop and gets fat, until his old world comes looking for him. Read from the closing, as a 9.
body:
9A 9 by its title: humanitarian & sage, and therefore the closing.

What it is

Yūto Suzuki's Sakamoto Days has run in Weekly Shōnen Jump since 2020. Tarō Sakamoto was once the most feared hitman in the underworld. Then he fell in love with a shop assistant, retired, married her and opened a convenience store. Years of happy family life have made him overweight and quiet. But a bounty is put on his head, and assassins start turning up at the shop.

How it works

Sakamoto has promised his wife never to kill again, so he fights using whatever is to hand: cash registers, shopping baskets, chopsticks and the shelves of his own store. He is joined by Shin, a former colleague who can read minds, and others he takes in, and the series grows into a war with the Order, an elite group of killers, and with a mysterious enemy from his past.

The action

Suzuki's fight scenes are among the most inventive in current manga, choreographed panel by panel like action cinema, with improvised weapons and surprising use of space. The domestic comedy of the shop balances the violence, and Sakamoto's devotion to his family drives everything.

Why it matters

It is one of the most popular Jump series of the 2020s and an example of the genre's turn towards adult heroes. A Netflix anime began in 2025.

title: Dr. Stone
synopsis: Every human on Earth is turned to stone, and a teenage genius who wakes 3,700 years later sets out to rebuild civilisation from scratch with science. 32 in the letters, reducing to 5.

What it is

Dr. Stone, written by Riichirō Inagaki and drawn by Boichi, ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 2017 to 2022 and was collected in 26 volumes. A mysterious flash of light turns every human being into stone. Senku Ishigami, a high-school student with an encyclopedic knowledge of science, stays conscious by counting the seconds, and breaks free about 3,700 years later into a world of forest and ruins.

How it works

Senku sets out to rebuild technology from nothing: fire, soap, iron, glass, antibiotics, electricity, radio and eventually far more. Each problem is solved step by step, with real chemistry and engineering explained along the way. His great rival is Tsukasa, a powerful fighter who wants to revive only the young and pure and keep the world free of the old civilisation.

The Kingdom of Science

Senku's friends, especially the villagers descended from survivors whom he meets, become his Kingdom of Science. The series' optimism is unusual: it argues that knowledge, shared and built upon over generations, is the most powerful force humans have.

Why it matters

It is a rare battle-free kind of shōnen hit, where the climaxes are inventions. Teachers praised it for making science exciting, and its anime, from 2019, was a major success.

title: The Promised Neverland
synopsis: Children at an idyllic orphanage discover that they are being raised as food, and plan an escape. Read from the pairing, as a 2.

What it is

The Promised Neverland, written by Kaiu Shirai and drawn by Posuka Demizu, ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 2016 to 2020 and was collected in 20 volumes. Grace Field House is a happy orphanage where children are cared for by a loving woman they call Mom, play in the woods and take daily tests. When one of them is sent away to be adopted, Emma and Norman, the brightest children, follow her to the gate and discover the truth: the orphanage is a farm, and its children are raised to be eaten by demons.

How it works

The first arc is a psychological thriller. Emma, Norman and Ray, the three oldest and cleverest children, plan an escape under the eyes of Mom, Isabella, who is as clever as they are and knows that they know. Every conversation is a test of trust and deception. Later arcs follow the children into the world beyond the wall.

The craft

Demizu's art, with its storybook detail, makes the house feel warm, and so makes the horror worse. Shirai builds the plot like a strategy game, and the children's refusal to abandon anyone, including the youngest, is what makes their plans so hard.

It brought a horror thriller to the heart of Jump and was a major international success. Its 2019 anime's first season was widely praised, while its second season, which departed sharply from the manga, was strongly criticised by fans.

title: Assassination Classroom
synopsis: A smiling, octopus-like creature that has destroyed most of the Moon becomes a class's teacher, and gives them a year to kill him before he destroys the Earth. Filed under 5, the turn.

What it is

Yūsei Matsui's Assassination Classroom ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 2012 to 2016 and was collected in 21 volumes. A yellow, tentacled creature that can move at twenty times the speed of sound has destroyed seventy per cent of the Moon. He announces that he will destroy the Earth next March, but first he wants to teach Class 3-E, the school's class of failures, at an elite junior high. The government offers the students a huge reward if they can kill him. They name him Koro-sensei.

The students plot and practise assassination attempts, with weapons supplied by the government that harm only him, and he dodges every one, while giving them the best education they have ever had. He teaches academic subjects, but also confidence, strategy and how to find their own strengths. Each student gets a chapter in which they find a talent.

The heart

The premise is a joke, but the story is about what a good teacher does. As the year passes, the students learn the truth about Koro-sensei's past, and the question becomes whether they can do what they were asked to do.

It was a major Jump hit, adapted as an anime and two live-action films, and is often recommended for its mix of comedy, action and emotional payoff. Many readers name its ending as one of the most moving in shōnen manga.

title: Blue Period
synopsis: A popular, bored high-school student discovers painting, and sets out to get into Japan's most competitive art university. 53 in the letters, reducing to 8.
body:
8The letters of this title total 53, an 8 — the number of money, authority, and the machinery of ambition.

What it is

Tsubasa Yamaguchi's Blue Period has run in Kodansha's Monthly Afternoon since 2017. Yatora Yaguchi is a high-school student who is good at everything: he gets top grades, stays out drinking with his friends and is liked by everyone. Yet he feels empty. When he sees a painting by an older student in the art room, and then tries to paint the blue light of Shibuya at dawn, he feels for the first time that he has communicated something real.

How it works

Yatora decides to apply to Tokyo University of the Arts, the most competitive art school in Japan, which accepts only a tiny fraction of applicants. The series follows his training: drawing exercises, composition, colour, critique and the brutal entrance exams. Real techniques and ways of thinking about art are explained in detail, and readers learn alongside him.

The characters

Yatora's classmates and rivals are drawn with care, especially Ryūji Ayukawa, who prefers to be called Yuka, and whose struggles with family and identity run alongside Yatora's. The series is honest about self-doubt and how hard it is to know whether you are good enough.

Why it matters

It won the Manga Taishō in 2020 and was adapted as an anime in 2021 and a live-action film in 2024. It is one of the best manga about learning an art, and has inspired many readers to pick up a brush.

title: Kaiju No. 8
synopsis: A 32-year-old who cleans up dead monsters for a living suddenly turns into one, just as he gets his last chance to join the force that fights them. Read from the closing, as a 9.
body:
9A 9 by its title: humanitarian & sage, and therefore the closing.

What it is

Naoya Matsumoto's Kaiju No. 8 ran on Shueisha's Shōnen Jump+ from 2020 to 2025. In a Japan regularly attacked by giant monsters, kaiju, the Defense Force fights them, and private companies clean up the bodies. Kafka Hibino, aged 32, works for one of those companies. As a boy he promised his friend Mina Ashiro that they would fight kaiju together. She became a famous captain; he failed the entrance exam and gave up.

How it works

A small creature enters Kafka's body, and he becomes able to transform into a powerful kaiju himself. The Defense Force names him Kaiju No. 8 and hunts him. At the same time, the age limit for recruits is raised, and he applies again. He must train and fight as a human while hiding that he is the monster they are looking for.

The hero

Kafka is unusual for a shōnen hero: an adult who had given up on his dream, and who is mocked for being too old. His story is about a second chance, and his relationship with the young recruits, especially the ambitious Reno Ichikawa, shows an older man encouraging the next generation.

Why it matters

It became one of the biggest hits of Jump+ and a major example of web serialisation reaching a mass audience. Its 2024 anime by Production I.G was widely watched around the world, and it draws on the long Japanese tradition of kaiju films and tokusatsu.

title: Barefoot Gen
synopsis: A boy in Hiroshima survives the atomic bomb that kills most of his family, and struggles to live in the ruined city that follows. Read from the closing, as a 9.
body:
9Nine — reckoning. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Keiji Nakazawa's Barefoot Gen began in Weekly Shōnen Jump in 1973 and, after it left Jump, continued in a series of smaller magazines until 1987. It was collected in 10 volumes. Gen Nakaoka is a boy in Hiroshima during the Second World War. His father, an artist, openly opposes the war, and the family is persecuted by neighbours and police as traitors. On 6 August 1945 the atomic bomb falls.

How it works

Gen's father, sister and younger brother are trapped under their burning house, and Gen and his pregnant mother cannot save them. The first volumes show the bombing and its immediate aftermath in unflinching detail: burned bodies, radiation sickness, starvation and the collapse of the city. Later volumes follow Gen through the occupation years, as he fights to survive, cares for orphans and grows up.

From life

The story is closely based on Nakazawa's own experience. He was six when the bomb fell, and lost his father, sister and brother in the same way. He had already told the story directly in a short autobiographical work, I Saw It (1972), before turning it into a long-form series.

Why it matters

It is one of the most important works of war testimony in any medium, and has been read by generations of Japanese schoolchildren. Volunteer translators carried it into English and many other languages, and its anime films (1983, 1986) brought it to more viewers. Its graphic violence and its criticism of the wartime emperor system have also made it the subject of repeated arguments over whether it belongs in school libraries.

title: Lone Wolf and Cub
synopsis: The shogun's executioner, framed and disgraced, wanders Edo-period Japan as an assassin for hire, pushing his infant son in a weaponised baby cart. Filed under 3, the telling.
body:
3The letters of this title total 57, a 3 — the number of communication, creativity, and the public stage.

What it is

Lone Wolf and Cub, written by Kazuo Koike and drawn by Goseki Kojima, ran in Futabasha's Weekly Manga Action from 1970 to 1976 and was collected in 28 volumes. Ogami Ittō was the shogun's official executioner until the scheming Yagyū clan murdered his wife and framed him for treason. Refusing to die, he takes his infant son Daigorō on the road to seek revenge, earning money as an assassin.

How it works

Most stories are self-contained episodes in which a client hires Ittō for a killing, which usually reveals something about the samurai code, the cruelty of the period or the lives of ordinary people. Daigorō rides in a wooden baby cart concealing blades and guns. Over the whole series runs the war between Ittō and the Yagyū, building to a final confrontation.

The art

Kojima's brushwork is restrained and cinematic, with long, nearly silent sequences of landscape, walking and sudden violence. Koike's scripts are full of historical detail about Edo-period customs, law and swordsmanship, and they give Daigorō's silent watching as much weight as his father's battles.

Why it matters

It is a masterpiece of gekiga and of samurai fiction. It was adapted into six films in the 1970s, which were later cut together abroad as Shogun Assassin, and its English edition in the 1980s, with covers by Frank Miller, introduced many American comics readers to manga. Its influence can be seen in later Western stories of a killer travelling with a child.

title: Glass Mask
synopsis: A poor, ordinary-looking girl with a genius for acting competes with a privileged rival for the right to play a legendary role. Read from the telling, as a 3.
body:
3A 3 by its title: creative communicator, and therefore the telling.

What it is

Suzue Miuchi's Glass Mask began in Hakusensha's Hana to Yume in 1976 and has been collected in 49 volumes, with its ending still unpublished. Maya Kitajima is a poor girl with no looks, no money and no talent anyone can see, except an extraordinary ability to become any role she plays. She is discovered by Chigusa Tsukikage, a once-great actress, who owns the rights to a legendary play, The Crimson Goddess.

How it works

Maya's rival is Ayumi Himekawa, the beautiful, gifted daughter of a famous actress and director, who has worked for everything she has. The two compete through stage plays, films and television towards the right to play the Crimson Goddess. Each arc is built around a performance, and Maya's process of finding a character is described in detail.

The romance

Maya is supported by an anonymous fan who sends her purple roses. He is secretly Masumi Hayami, the cold head of a talent agency who seems to be her enemy. The slow, painful romance between them is one of the most famous in shōjo manga.

Why it matters

It is one of the best-selling shōjo manga ever and a classic of the genre's grand melodrama. It has been adapted as anime, television drama and stage plays, and its intense rivalry and dedication to art remain models for later stories about performers.

title: Candy Candy
altTitles: キャンディ・キャンディ
synopsis: A cheerful orphan in early twentieth-century America meets love, loss and hardship, and never stops smiling. The title reduces to 4 — the structure.
body:
4A 4 by its title: builder & organizer, and therefore the structure.

What it is

Candy Candy, written by Kyōko Mizuki and drawn by Yumiko Igarashi, ran in Kodansha's Nakayoshi from 1975 to 1979 and was collected in 9 volumes. Candice White is a freckled, tomboyish orphan raised at the Pony's Home in the American Midwest in the early twentieth century. Taken in as a companion by the wealthy, cruel Leagan family, she meets the people who will shape her life.

How it works

The story follows Candy from childhood through an English boarding school to training as a nurse during the First World War. It is full of melodrama: the death of her first love, Anthony, a doomed romance with the rebellious Terry, and the mystery of her protector, the Prince of the Hill. Through every disaster Candy remains brave and kind.

The style

Igarashi's art is the classic 1970s shōjo look: huge sparkling eyes, flowing hair, flowers and elaborate period costume. Mizuki's story draws on Western children's literature, from Anne of Green Gables to Daddy-Long-Legs.

Why it matters

It was a huge hit, and its 1976 anime spread it across Europe, Latin America and Asia. A long legal dispute between its two creators over the rights, settled by Japan's Supreme Court in 2001 in Mizuki's favour as co-author, has kept the manga out of print for years.

title: Crayon Shin-chan
synopsis: A rude, shameless five-year-old in the Tokyo suburbs torments his parents, his friends and everyone else, and is somehow lovable. Filed under 8, the ledger.

What it is

Yoshito Usui's Crayon Shin-chan began in Futabasha's Weekly Manga Action in 1990 and later moved to Manga Town, running until 2010 and filling 50 volumes. Shinnosuke Nohara, known as Shin-chan, is a five-year-old in Kasukabe, a commuter town in Saitama Prefecture. He flirts with grown women, does a rude dance with his bottom, says exactly what he thinks and drives his parents, Misae and Hiroshi, to despair.

How it works

The strips and short chapters are mostly gags about family life, kindergarten and the neighbourhood. Shin-chan's mother struggles with housework and money, his father with his job and his feet, and the comedy comes from a child's misunderstandings of adult life. It was published in a magazine for adults, and many of the jokes are for them.

A family story

Under the crudeness, the Noharas are a loving, ordinary middle-class family, and the series, especially its films, often turns to warm stories about parents and children.

Why it matters

Its anime, running since 1992, made Shin-chan one of Japan's most famous characters, and its annual films are hugely popular. Usui died in an accident while hiking in 2009, and his assistants continued the series as New Crayon Shin-chan from 2010.

title: Chibi Maruko-chan
synopsis: A lazy, daydreaming girl in 1970s Shizuoka lives an ordinary childhood with her family and classmates, based on the author's own. 73 in the letters, reducing to 1.

1Title sums to 73 and reduces to 1 — The Opening, where the reference files a first move.

What it is

Momoko Sakura's Chibi Maruko-chan began in Shueisha's girls' magazine Ribon in 1986 and ran there regularly until 1996, with occasional chapters afterwards. Momoko Sakura, nicknamed Maruko, is a third-grader in the town of Shimizu, in Shizuoka Prefecture, in the 1970s. She is lazy, greedy and fond of daydreaming, and lives with her parents, her older sister and her grandparents.

How it works

Each chapter is a small episode of childhood: a school trip, a festival, a craze for a pop idol, an argument with her sister, a scheme to avoid homework. The characters are her real family and classmates, gently exaggerated. A narrator comments on Maruko's behaviour with dry, adult humour.

Nostalgia

The series is set a decade or more before it was written, and recreates the details of 1970s childhood: television shows, snacks, toys and the rhythms of family life. Readers who grew up then found their own memories in it, and younger readers found an ordinary past.

Why it matters

Its anime, broadcast from 1990, became a national hit, and its theme song was a best-seller. It remains on television, and Maruko is one of the most familiar characters in Japan. Sakura, who also wrote best-selling essays, died in 2018.

title: Saint Young Men
synopsis: Jesus and the Buddha take a holiday on Earth, sharing a cheap flat in the Tokyo suburbs and trying to live like ordinary young men. The title reduces to 6 — the care.
body:
6Filed under 6. The Care takes an obligation, and this entry is protects one.

What it is

Hikaru Nakamura's Saint Young Men has run in Kodansha's Morning magazines since 2006. Jesus and the Buddha, after centuries of hard work, take a holiday on Earth. They rent a small apartment together in Tachikawa, a suburb of Tokyo, and live on a tight budget, shopping, going to the bathhouse, blogging and trying not to be recognised.

How it works

The comedy comes from two of the most important figures in human history dealing with ordinary modern life. Jesus loves shopping and blogs; the Buddha is careful with money and draws manga. Their miracles happen by accident: Jesus turns bathwater into wine when he relaxes, and animals gather around the Buddha. Many jokes depend on details from the Bible and the Buddhist scriptures.

The tone

The series is affectionate rather than mocking. Jesus and the Buddha are kind, good friends and very funny, and it pokes fun at modern Japanese life more than at religion. Other figures, including saints, archangels and Buddhist deities, visit them.

Why it matters

It became a best-seller and was adapted as an anime film (2013) and live-action productions. It is a much-loved example of gentle comedy built on an outrageous premise, and Nakamura's other major work, Arakawa Under the Bridge, shares its warm absurdity.

title: Thermae Romae
synopsis: An ancient Roman architect who designs public baths keeps slipping through time into modern Japan, and takes its bathing ideas home. The title reduces to 5 — the turn.
body:
5Five — change. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Mari Yamazaki's Thermae Romae ran in Enterbrain's Comic Beam from 2008 to 2013 and was collected in 6 volumes. Lucius Quintus Modestus is an architect in Rome in the time of the emperor Hadrian, who designs public baths and worries that his ideas are out of date. One day, while bathing, he is sucked down a drain and emerges in a public bathhouse in modern Japan.

How it works

Each episode follows the same pattern. Lucius is transported to Japan, sees an ordinary bathing invention, such as a bottled drink after a bath, a home bathtub or a hot spring resort, believes it is the work of a remarkable slave people he calls the "flat-faced tribe", and takes the idea back to Rome, where it makes him famous.

The comedy

The joke is the collision of two bath cultures, ancient Roman and modern Japanese, and of Lucius's serious amazement at things the reader takes for granted. Yamazaki, who studied in Italy, draws Roman history and architecture in detail, and the series is full of real information about both cultures.

Why it matters

It won the Manga Taishō and the Tezuka Osamu Cultural Prize Short Story Award in 2010. Its live-action films starring Hiroshi Abe (2012, 2014) were hits, and it is one of the best-known examples of time-slip comedy in manga.

title: Kamui Den
synopsis: In Edo-period Japan, an outcast boy becomes a ninja, while peasants and a samurai struggle against a cruel feudal order. Read from the teaching, as a 33.
body:
33Thirty-three — service. That is the reduction of this title, and the shelf it is read from.

What it is

Sanpei Shirato's Kamui Den ran from 1964 to 1971 in Garo, a monthly magazine founded largely to publish it, with a second part following in the 1980s and 1990s. Set in the Edo period, it follows three young men from different classes: Kamui, born into the lowest caste of outcasts, who becomes a ninja to escape it; Shōsuke, a peasant who leads his village against oppression; and Ryūnosuke, a samurai whose family is destroyed by intrigue.

How it works

The story is an epic of the feudal system seen from below. It shows famine, taxation, uprisings, discrimination against outcasts and the violence of those in power, and it follows how the three men's lives cross. Much of it is about economics and class: how rice is grown, how it is taxed, and who suffers.

The politics

Shirato, the son of a left-wing painter, wrote Kamui Den as a Marxist history, and it was read eagerly by the student radicals of the 1960s. Its seriousness about history and society helped show that manga could be political literature.

Why it matters

It made Garo the home of alternative manga, which went on to publish artists such as Yoshiharu Tsuge, and it is one of the landmarks of gekiga. A separate, more action-centred story about Kamui, Kamui Gaiden, was adapted as an anime and as a live-action film.

title: Kimagure Orange Road
altTitles: きまぐれオレンジ☆ロード
synopsis: A teenage boy from a family of secret psychics is caught between a cool, mysterious girl and her cheerful best friend. The title reduces to 3 — the telling.
body:
3A 3 by its title: creative communicator, and therefore the telling.

What it is

Izumi Matsumoto's Kimagure Orange Road ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1984 to 1987 and was collected in 18 volumes. Kyōsuke Kasuga is an indecisive high-school student whose family has psychic powers that they must keep hidden. After moving to a new town, he meets Madoka Ayukawa, a beautiful, cool girl with a reputation as a delinquent, and falls for her, only for her younger friend Hikaru to fall for him.

How it works

The series is a romantic comedy built on a love triangle. Kyōsuke cannot bring himself to hurt Hikaru or to tell Madoka how he feels, and his attempts to keep everyone happy make things worse. His family's powers, such as teleportation and moving objects, create comic emergencies and allow occasional fantasy episodes.

The mood

Matsumoto drew with soft, stylish art, and the series has a gentle, bittersweet atmosphere of summer, music and adolescence. Madoka, who plays the saxophone and hides her kindness behind a tough front, became one of the most iconic heroines of the 1980s.

Why it matters

It was one of the defining romantic comedies of 1980s shōnen manga, and its anime, from 1987, became a cult favourite abroad. It influenced many later love-triangle stories. Matsumoto's later career was limited by serious health problems.

title: Blade of the Immortal
synopsis: A samurai cursed with immortality agrees to help a girl avenge her parents, as penance for the lives he has taken. Filed under 8, the ledger.
body:
8Title sums to 80 and reduces to 8 — The Ledger, where the reference files a reckoning.

What it is

Hiroaki Samura's Blade of the Immortal ran in Kodansha's Monthly Afternoon from 1993 to 2012 and was collected in 30 volumes. Manji is a rōnin who has killed a hundred men, among them his sister's husband. A mysterious old nun puts sacred bloodworms into his body, and now any wound he takes heals: severed limbs reattach and he cannot die. To lift the curse, he vows to kill a thousand evil men.

How it works

Rin Asano, a girl whose father was murdered and mother taken by a group of swordsmen called the Ittō-ryū, hires Manji as her bodyguard for revenge. Their journey through Edo-period Japan brings them into conflict with the Ittō-ryū, led by the charismatic Anotsu Kagehisa, who wants to destroy the old schools of swordsmanship, and with the government forces who hunt them all.

The art

Samura's art is one of the series' great strengths. He alternates between rough pencil sketches, detailed ink drawing and sudden explosions of motion, and his fights are fast, chaotic and bloody. His characters wear a mix of period clothing and anachronistic style, giving the world a punk edge.

Why it matters

It is one of the most admired samurai manga, praised for its art and its moral complexity: almost every swordsman has a reason, and revenge is never simple. Its English edition won an Eisner Award in 2000, and Takashi Miike adapted it as a film in 2017.
