title: Emma
synopsis: In Victorian London, a quiet maid and the son of a wealthy merchant family fall in love across the barriers of class. Filed under 5, the turn.
body:
5Reduced, this title gives 5. It sits on The Turn with the rest of a turn.

What it is

Kaoru Mori's Emma ran in Enterbrain's Comic Beam from 2002, with its main story ending in 2006 and further stories about its characters continuing until 2008. It was collected in 10 volumes. Emma is a maid working for a retired governess in London at the end of the nineteenth century. William Jones, the heir to a newly rich merchant family and a former pupil of her employer, visits and falls in love with her.

How it works

The romance is slow and restrained. William's family expects him to marry into the aristocracy, and the gap between a maid and a gentleman is enormous. Emma is reserved and practical, and the story follows both of them as they decide what they are willing to give up.

The detail

Mori is famous for her love of Victorian Britain, and the series is full of carefully researched detail: costume, servants' work, households, trains, the Crystal Palace. The lives of the servants are given as much care as those of their employers.

Why it matters

It received an Excellence Prize at the Japan Media Arts Festival and was adapted as an anime in 2005. It is one of the most admired historical romances in manga and the work that first showed the patient, detailed style Mori developed further in A Bride's Story.

title: Ah! My Goddess
synopsis: An unlucky college student dials a wrong number and reaches a goddess, who grants him a wish, and he wishes that she would stay with him forever. Filed under 3, the telling.
body:

What it is

Kōsuke Fujishima's Ah! My Goddess ran in Kodansha's Monthly Afternoon from 1988 to 2014 and was collected in 48 volumes. Keiichi Morisato is a shy, unlucky engineering student who lives in a cramped men's dormitory. Trying to order food by phone, he accidentally calls the Goddess Relief Office, and a goddess named Belldandy appears in his room to grant him one wish. Half joking, he wishes that a goddess like her would stay with him forever. The wish is granted.

How it works

Keiichi and Belldandy move into an old temple and are soon joined by her sisters: Urd, a seductive troublemaker, and Skuld, a young inventor who resents Keiichi. Most stories are comedy episodes about magic, mechanics and misunderstandings, while longer arcs involve demons, rival gods and the system of heaven itself.

The craft

Fujishima is a devoted motorcycle and car enthusiast, and the machines Keiichi rebuilds with his university motor club are drawn with great precision. His art evolved enormously over the long run, from rounded 1980s figures to an elegant, detailed style.

Why it matters

It is a classic of the gentle romantic comedy, with a devoted couple and very little conflict between them. Its anime adaptations, beginning with a 1993 original video series, made Belldandy an icon, and the series influenced many later stories in which a magical girl moves in with an ordinary young man.

title: Shaman King
synopsis: A laid-back boy who can see spirits enters a tournament held every five hundred years to decide the king of all shamans. 43 in the letters, reducing to 7.
body:
7Title sums to 43 and reduces to 7 — The Inquiry, where the reference files an open question.

What it is

Hiroyuki Takei's Shaman King ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 1998 to 2004 and was collected in 32 volumes. Yoh Asakura is a relaxed, easygoing boy from a family of shamans, people who can see and communicate with spirits. He moves to Tokyo with the ghost of a samurai who died six hundred years earlier, Amidamaru, who becomes his partner in battle.

How it works

Every five hundred years, shamans from around the world fight in the Shaman Fight to decide who will become the Shaman King, able to reshape the world. Shamans fight by merging with their spirits, and each has a distinct style drawn from a different culture or religion. Yoh's strict fiancée, Anna, trains him, and he gathers friends from around the world, while his twin brother Hao threatens to win and destroy humanity.

Its ending

The original serialisation ended abruptly in 2004. Takei finished the story in a complete edition published in 2008 and 2009, adding the final chapters he had planned, and later wrote sequels.

Why it matters

It was one of Jump's major hits around 2000, and its anime, from 2001, and a remake in 2021 brought it to audiences worldwide. Its idea of fighting through partnerships with spirits, and its celebration of many cultures, are its lasting signatures.

title: Fairy Tail
synopsis: A young wizard joins a rowdy, close-knit guild of magic users and takes on jobs, rivals and dark guilds alongside a fire-eating dragon slayer. 47 in the letters, reducing to 11.
body:
11The letters of this title total 47, an 11 — the number of inspiration, tension, and heightened awareness.

What it is

Hiro Mashima's Fairy Tail ran in Kodansha's Weekly Shōnen Magazine from 2006 to 2017 and was collected in 63 volumes. In the kingdom of Fiore, wizards belong to guilds that take on jobs for pay. Lucy Heartfilia, a young celestial wizard who can summon spirits with magical keys, dreams of joining Fairy Tail, the most notorious guild of all. She is brought there by Natsu Dragneel, a fire-eating dragon slayer, and his flying blue cat, Happy.

How it works

The series alternates between comic jobs and long arcs against dark guilds, tournaments and ancient dragons. Each guild member has a distinctive magic, and the story places great weight on loyalty: when one member is hurt, the whole guild goes to war. Natsu, Lucy, the ice wizard Gray and the armoured swordswoman Erza form its central team.

The appeal

Mashima's art is bright and energetic, and the series is driven by friendship, found family and big emotional speeches. It does not aim for subtlety, and its directness was a large part of its popularity.

Why it matters

It was one of the most popular shōnen series of its time, especially outside Japan, and its long-running anime made it a gateway to manga for many readers. Mashima followed it with Edens Zero.

title: Soul Eater
synopsis: At a school run by Death himself, students who can turn into weapons and the partners who wield them hunt corrupted souls. Read from the ledger, as an 8.

8An 8 by its title: visionary & achiever, and therefore the ledger.

What it is

Atsushi Ōkubo's Soul Eater ran in Square Enix's Monthly Shōnen Gangan from 2004 to 2013 and was collected in 25 volumes. In Death City, Lord Death runs an academy for two kinds of students: weapons, people who can transform into blades, guns and other arms, and meisters, who wield them. Maka Albarn, a serious, studious meister, is partnered with Soul Eater, a laid-back boy who becomes a scythe.

How it works

To turn Soul into a Death Scythe, a weapon worthy of Lord Death himself, the pair must collect the souls of 99 evil humans and one witch. They train and fight alongside their classmates, including the loud ninja Black Star and Death's own son, Death the Kid, who is obsessed with symmetry. The series grows into a war against witches and an ancient being of madness.

The style

Ōkubo's art is gothic and playful, with grinning moons and suns, sharp shapes and fashionable characters. Madness, fear and courage are central themes, and the comedy and horror sit side by side.

Why it matters

Its 2008 anime by Studio Bones made it a worldwide hit, and its partnership between weapon and wielder, where each relies on the other's soul, is its most memorable idea. Ōkubo went on to create Fire Force.

title: Wandering Son
synopsis: Two transgender children, a boy who wants to be a girl and a girl who wants to be a boy, grow up together from primary school to adulthood. 62 in the letters, reducing to 8.
body:
8The letters of this title total 62, an 8 — the number of money, authority, and the machinery of ambition.

What it is

Takako Shimura's Wandering Son ran in Enterbrain's Comic Beam from 2002 to 2013 and was collected in 15 volumes. Shūichi Nitori is a gentle fifth-grader, assigned male at birth, who wants to be a girl. Yoshino Takatsuki, a new classmate, is assigned female and wants to be a boy. They recognise something in each other and become close friends.

How it works

The story follows them and their classmates from primary school through puberty to the end of high school. Puberty brings changes that both dread. Shūichi experiments with dressing as a girl in public and faces the reactions of family, friends and strangers. Around them, other characters explore their own identities and feelings, including first loves.

The tone

Shimura writes with great tenderness and restraint. There is no melodrama: the series observes ordinary days, small cruelties and quiet acts of support. Its watercolour-soft art and gentle pace make it feel like a coming-of-age diary.

Why it matters

It is one of the most respected manga about transgender youth, praised for its honesty and care. It was adapted as an anime in 2011, and its English edition introduced many readers to Shimura's work, including the yuri romance Sweet Blue Flowers.

synopsis: Two office workers who are both secret otaku, a fujoshi and a hardcore gamer, start dating and try to be adults about it. 116 in the letters, reducing to 8.

What it is

Fujita's Wotakoi: Love Is Hard for Otaku began as a webcomic posted on the illustration site pixiv in 2014, and was then serialised on Ichijinsha's web magazine Comic Pool until 2021, collected in 11 volumes. Narumi Momose has changed jobs to escape the fallout when her last boyfriend found out she was an otaku. At her new office she finds her childhood friend Hirotaka Nifuji, a quiet, devoted gamer.

How it works

Narumi, a fujoshi who loves boys' love manga, and Hirotaka, who plays games every spare moment, start dating, mostly because neither has to hide anything from the other. The episodes are short comic scenes from their relationship, their hobbies and their workplace, along with another couple, their colleagues Hanako and Tarō, who are also otaku.

The comedy

The series is full of fan in-jokes: game terms, convention habits, the particular language of BL fans. But its heart is an adult relationship between two people who are comfortable with each other, and it treats the characters' passions with affection rather than mockery.

Why it matters

It is a well-known example of a manga that began on pixiv and became a major hit. Its 2018 anime and 2020 live-action film made it popular with adult fans who saw themselves in it.

title: Erased
synopsis: A struggling manga artist who is sometimes sent back in time to prevent disasters is thrown back eighteen years to save a classmate from a serial killer. 25 in the letters, reducing to 7.

What it is

Kei Sanbe's Erased, whose Japanese title means "the town where only I am missing", ran in Kadokawa's Young Ace from 2012 to 2016. Satoru Fujinuma is a 29-year-old manga artist who delivers pizzas to make ends meet. He has a strange ability he calls Revival: when something terrible is about to happen, he is sent back a few minutes in time and can prevent it.

How it works

When his mother is murdered and he is blamed, Revival throws Satoru back eighteen years, to 1988, into his eleven-year-old body in a snowy town in Hokkaido. That winter, a classmate, Kayo Hinazuki, was abducted and killed, the first of a series of murders. Satoru realises that if he can save her, he may change everything that followed.

The heart

The mystery of the killer drives the plot, but the most moving parts are about Kayo, who is abused by her mother, and Satoru's efforts as a child, with an adult's mind, to protect her and befriend her. The series treats child abuse and loneliness with seriousness.

Why it matters

It was a major success, adapted as an anime and a live-action film in 2016 and as a Netflix series in 2017. Its combination of time travel, mystery and emotional drama made it one of the most discussed thrillers of its time.

title: The Disastrous Life of Saiki K.
synopsis: A boy born with every psychic power imaginable wants only one thing: to be left alone and live a normal, unremarkable life. Read from the telling, as a 3.
body:
3Filed under 3. The Telling takes an act of telling, and this entry is renders one.

What it is

Shūichi Asō's The Disastrous Life of Saiki K. ran in Weekly Shōnen Jump from 2012 to 2018 and was collected in 26 volumes. Kusuo Saiki was born with every psychic power: telepathy, telekinesis, teleportation, X-ray vision and more. He could rule the world. Instead, he finds his powers exhausting and wants only to live an unremarkable life, keep a low profile at school and eat coffee jelly.

How it works

Each chapter is a short comic episode in which Saiki's plans for a quiet life are wrecked by his classmates: the cheerful idiot Nendō, whose mind Saiki cannot read because he thinks nothing; the chūnibyō Kaidō, who believes he fights a secret war; and Teruhashi, the perfect girl who cannot believe he is not in love with her. Saiki's deadpan inner monologue narrates his suffering.

The joke

The series inverts the power fantasy. Saiki's powers make life worse, not better: reading every thought is noisy and disappointing, and every miracle makes it harder to be ordinary. He constantly uses godlike abilities for trivial ends.

Why it matters

Its anime, from 2016, became popular internationally, and it was adapted as a live-action film in 2017. It is one of the best Jump gag manga of its era and a sharp parody of the psychic-hero genre.
